subject.title: feat: add Podman agent sandbox backend

question: Should `sandbox.allowBackends: ["docker"]` intentionally authorize native Podman whenever Docker is absent, or must Podman require its own explicit authorization identity?
rationale: The PR changes which engine enforces agent isolation without changing user configuration, so maintainers must define whether the policy identity represents a container-backend family or one exact engine.

options.title: Authorize container family
options.body: Keep Docker-first Podman fallback, document that `docker` policy authorizes either local engine, and enforce identical runtime and doctor validation.

options.title: Require explicit Podman
options.body: Expose Podman as a distinct configured and policy-authorized backend so engine selection is never implicit.

options.title: Defer Podman support
options.body: Pause the change until a narrower sandbox-engine authorization contract is designed and approved.

recommendation.title: Authorize container family
recommendation.body: Keep Docker-first Podman fallback, document that `docker` policy authorizes either local engine, and enforce identical runtime and doctor validation.

likelyOwner.reason: Authored the final fallback architecture and most directly owns the current container-engine boundary.
